Time_Annotation: The report notes that 'another tropical depression formed east of the Chagos Archipelago on January 3' and later states that the 'remnants of Bonita continued across Africa, emerging into the southern Atlantic Ocean on January 19 and dissipating the next day,' marking the end of the event.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: The article mentions that Bonita made landfall about 50 km north of Foulpointe in eastern Madagascar (with heavy damage and fatalities), later made a second landfall in eastern Mozambique between Pebane and Quelimane, and its remnants brought the heaviest rainfall in 80 years to eastern Zimbabwe with additional heavy rainfall spreading into Zambia.
Main_Event_Annotation: The system was first noted as a tropical depression but then 'strengthened into Tropical Storm Bonita' on January 5 and 'three days later reached tropical cyclone status as it developed a well-defined eye,' indicating it falls under the Tropical Storm/Cyclone category.
Hazards_Annotation: The cyclone produced gusts exceeding 230 km/h as noted in eastern Madagascar and caused widespread flooding—evidenced by 24‑hour rainfall totals of 170 mm at Toamasina, widespread damage to crops and infrastructure in Madagascar and Mozambique, and heavy rainfall impacts in Zimbabwe and Zambia.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: It then crossed Interstate 24 at Spring Street and produced major EF3-strength damage in East Nashville, specifically in the Five Points neighborhood, where numerous businesses, restaurants, bars, homes, and apartment buildings were damaged or destroyed. Notable structures included Basement East (a popular music venue), a badly damaged YMCA, and a completely destroyed Dollar General store.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: described in text without a specific number
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The tornado soon moved into Donelson, crossing the Stones River twice and destroying much of Donelson Christian Academy and the Stanford Estates subdivision. Numerous homes at Stanford Estates were destroyed, vehicles were thrown and mangled, and a few homes were leveled at high-end EF3 strength.

The tornado moved through Mount Juliet, producing a large swath of high-end EF3 damage as it crossed North Mount Juliet Road. It substantially damaged Mount Juliet Christian Academy, West Wilson Middle School, and Stoner Creek Elementary, and numerous homes throughout town were heavily damaged or destroyed—with some completely leveled.

In Lebanon, many homes and businesses suffered considerable damage. The damage included losses at two large cemeteries, Lebanon Municipal Airport, Walmart, and Lowe's, while a gas station and a heavy equipment auctioneer’s property sustained low-end EF2 damage with a blown canopy and knocked-down exterior walls.

As it crossed ridges and valleys through southern Gordonsville—particularly along Agee Branch Road, Hickman Highway, and Maple Street—there was notable tree and structural damage, though no specific building count is given.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The tornado reached EF1 intensity as it crossed Highway 56 and moved through a residential subdivision. It caused minor to moderate roof damage to numerous homes and destroyed an outbuilding.
The tornado intensified to EF2 strength as it crossed Prosperity Drive, tearing the roof and exterior walls off a home.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: numerous homes and a garage structure
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Entering the community of Double Springs, the tornado heavily damaged or destroyed numerous homes and a garage structure at EF2 to EF3 strength, before cutting a narrow swath of intense damage across Bloomington Road, Clemmons Road, and Charlton Square.
As the tornado crossed Charlton Square in the eastern part of the Eller Plantation subdivision, two homes were swept away.
Numerous other nearby homes in the subdivision were also damaged or destroyed.
Numerous fatalities occurred as at least 17 well-anchored block-foundation homes were leveled or swept away along Hensley Drive and North McBroom Chapel Road.
Continuing eastward, the tornado continued to produce EF4 damage as it leveled a large apartment building along the north side of U.S. 70N.
Just east of this point, additional EF4 damage occurred in the Echo Valley subdivision, where many homes were leveled or swept away.
The tornado continued along U.S. 70N, weakening to high-end EF3 strength as it flattened the Echo Valley Market, a local convenience store.
EF3-strength damage continued as it impacted residential areas within the vicinity of South Drive and Locust Grove Road, damaging or destroying multiple homes.

Locations: vicinity of South Drive and Locust Grove Road
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: a few poorly-anchored homes, a small apartment building, a metal structure, and outbuildings
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A few poorly-anchored homes were leveled or swept from their foundations along this segment of the path, while a small apartment building, a metal structure, and outbuildings also sustained significant damage.
Several metal storage unit buildings were destroyed in this area as well.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: a smoke shop and a metal-framed warehouse structure
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The tornado weakened further to EF2 intensity as it crossed Tennessee Avenue and Miller Road, badly damaging a smoke shop and a metal-framed warehouse structure.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: mobile homes and outbuildings destroyed, and numerous frame homes damaged
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Significant damage continued as the tornado moved due-east, following West Broad Street (U.S. 70N). Mobile homes and outbuildings were destroyed, and numerous frame homes were damaged, some of which sustained roof and exterior wall loss.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: a few businesses and other structures, including a bank and the Upper Cumberland Electric Membership Corporation
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: A few businesses and other structures, including a bank and the Upper Cumberland Electric Membership Corporation, also sustained considerable damage as the tornado entered the Cookeville city limits.
A majority of the damage along this corridor was rated EF2, though a small pocket of low-end EF3 damage occurred near County Farm Road, where a poorly-anchored home was swept away.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: an Exxon gas station severely damaged, and a small used car dealership leveled and swept away
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: At the intersection of Pippin Road and West Jackson Street with West Broad Street, an Exxon gas station was severely damaged, and a small used car dealership across the street was leveled and swept away, with only the basement of the building remaining. This damage was given a high-end EF2 rating.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: homes and other structures with minor to moderate damage
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Continuing towards downtown Cookeville, the tornado passed south of Sycamore Elementary School, downing trees and causing minor to moderate damage to homes and other structures at EF0 to EF1 strength.

Locations: areas just east of Buck Avenue
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: trees, some apartment buildings, and homes damaged
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Additional EF0 to EF1 damage to trees, some apartment buildings, and homes occurred as the tornado crossed Buck Avenue and moved through areas just east of this point.
